sh: Nvidia beats forecasts after CEO exit
headline: Nvidia’s sales double and beat forecasts in its first results since its CEO quit
summary: Nvidia reported revenue of $115.8 billion for the three months to 25 October, up 103% from a year earlier, on Tuesday 17 November. It forecast sales above analysts’ estimates for the next quarter, in its first results since chief executive Jensen Huang resigned.
why: Nvidia makes most of the chips used to build artificial intelligence, so its results show whether the AI boom is still going. They came after a week of turmoil over its leadership and a sharp fall in US tech stocks.

event.t: Revenue was $115.8 billion in the quarter to 25 October, up 103% from a year earlier. Revenue from data centres, mostly AI chips, was $107.6 billion.

Nvidia expects about $130 billion in revenue next quarter, plus or minus 3%. Analysts had expected $125.25 billion on average, Reuters reports, citing LSEG data. The forecast assumes no sales of data-centre chips in China.
Interim chief executive Colette Kress said the company’s “momentum is real”. The Washington Post notes the results did little to answer questions about Nvidia’s future after Huang’s exit.

Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia’s chief executive on Thursday 12 November, the company’s board said. It followed reports of affairs, including one with a woman US intelligence agencies suspect of spying for China.
Chief financial officer Colette Kress is interim chief executive while the company looks for a permanent replacement.
On Monday 16 November the S&P 500 fell 1.9% and the Nasdaq 2.5%. Nvidia shares fell 4.1% to $156.14, their lowest close since July 2025, CNN reports.

effects.label: AI industry
effects.t: Record sales and a higher forecast show demand for AI chips is still growing.

effects.label: Wall Street
effects.t: Stocks fell sharply on Tuesday before the results; the S&P 500 had its lowest close since late July.

updates.t: US stocks fell again on Tuesday before the results. At 15:15 GMT the S&P 500 was down 0.32%, the Dow 0.68% and the Nasdaq 0.16%, AFP reported, and the losses grew later in the morning.
Before the results, the S&P 500 closed down 1.03% at 7,340.53, its lowest close since late July. The Dow fell 848.75 points, or 1.64%, and the Nasdaq 0.74%.
Nvidia reports revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier, and forecasts about $130 billion for next quarter, above analysts’ estimates.
updates.why: The results show demand for AI chips is still strong despite the leadership crisis.

updates.t: On the earnings call, board chair Harvey Jones said the board has no intention of bringing Jensen Huang back as chief executive. Nvidia shares rose in trading after the market closed.
updates.why: It answers the question of whether Huang could quickly return to lead the company.

updates.t: In Asia on Wednesday, South Korea’s Kospi led early gains as chipmakers rose on Nvidia’s forecast, CNBC reports.
Nvidia shares rose early on Wednesday but the gains faded and the stock turned lower, as Wall Street kept swinging on doubts about the AI boom.

Jensen Huang agreed to answer questions from three House committees on 1 December about possible Chinese spying and breaches of US chip export rules; Nvidia’s general counsel Tim Teter is due on 2 December. Senate Banking Committee chair Tim Scott said Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick have also agreed to appear before his committee, which he hopes will happen before Christmas.
updates.why: It will be the first time Huang answers lawmakers’ questions since he resigned.

updates.t: US stocks closed mostly lower on Wednesday. The S&P 500 fell 0.23% to 7,323.63, its fifth loss in a row, and the Dow fell 561 points, or 1.11%, while the Nasdaq rose 0.42%. Nvidia’s strong results did not lift AI stocks, Investrade notes, as fears of Fed rate rises weighed on markets.
